title: Master Circular on Health Insurance Products
source_doc: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Products
summary_en: Consolidates and repeals 55 earlier circulars and sets policyholder-friendly norms, including cashless timelines.

title: Cashless authorisation timelines
source_doc: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Products (2024)
ref: IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/5/2024; paragraph number to be confirmed
summary_en: The insurer decides on cashless pre-authorisation within 1 hour and on final discharge authorisation within 3 hours of the hospital's request.

title: Norms on proportionate deductions
summary_en: Proportionate deduction may apply only to defined associated medical expenses when a higher room category is chosen. Pharmacy and consumables, implants and medical devices, and diagnostics are excluded from associated expenses, and no proportionate deduction applies to ICU charges.

title: Pre-existing disease: look-back and maximum waiting period
source_doc: IRDAI health insurance norms effective 1 April 2024
ref: PED definition and waiting periods, effective 1 April 2024
summary_en: The PED look-back is 36 months (was 48). The maximum PED waiting period is 36 months, and specific waiting periods are capped at 36 months.

title: Moratorium period
source_doc: IRDAI health insurance norms effective 1 April 2024
summary_en: After 60 months of continuous cover (was 96), the insurer cannot contest a claim or the policy for non-disclosure or misrepresentation, except proven fraud.

title: Non-payable items: Annexure I, Lists I to IV
source_doc: IRDAI standardisation guidelines, Annexure I (carried into the Master Circular)
ref: Annexure I, Lists I-IV; item list to be loaded from the official PDF
summary_en: List I items are not payable unless the insurer offers an optional cover. List II, III and IV items are subsumed into room, procedure and treatment cost respectively, so they are not separate deductions.

title: Insurer grievance resolution timeline
ref: Insurer grievance timeline; 14 or 15 days to be confirmed
summary_en: The insurer should resolve a written grievance within 15 days.

title: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended)
summary_en: Complain to the Ombudsman after the insurer rejects a written complaint, replies unsatisfactorily, or does not reply within 1 month; file within 1 year; claim value up to 50 lakh; free of cost; the award binds the insurer.

title: Bima Bharosa grievance portal
summary_en: Open to all with no claim-amount limit; forwards the complaint to the insurer and tracks it.
